title: Redesign the Stream, Not the Role
notes_html:
Start with a tiger team. One or two small teams on one stream move faster, give you a safe place to test new incentives and roles, and avoid pushing change on everyone at once.

Data is usually the hidden barrier. Mapping the stream often shows that the data feeding it is the biggest obstacle - and the biggest unlock. See Avoid the Naughty List when it's ready.

A moved bottleneck is progress. Every line manager knows this: fix the constraint, it moves, fix the next one. You just have to know where it is first - which is why you map the stream.

The invisible work shows up on the map. The handoffs, the re-keying and the person everyone calls are exactly what Automate the Invisible goes after, and the know-how Embed the Expert protects.

Inspired by Sandra Loughlin, PhD Chief Learning Scientist at EPAM. Her argument that AI work redesign should start from the value stream, not the role - and that roles are redesigned last - is the heart of this pattern.
strip: Paste this into any AI system's custom instructions or at the start of a conversation to run Pattern 21. It maps one end-to-end process with you, finds where the work actually waits, and redesigns the flow before anyone's role changes.
